items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: And he had Albert Glenny on the bass. And that's right, that was his band.

ctx.x: Yeah, I never heard him. Why couldn't he, uh, couldn't he play for his heart?

No, he couldn't. After the doctor told him he had heart trouble, he had to put that trumpet down, that was all. He couldn't go to the top? No, he said he wasn't gonna take no chance. But they got a lot of fellas that got heart trouble and still playing. But not him, he wasn't gonna take no chance. And he's still living ever since he put that horn down. He just put a ribbon around him, put it on top of his piano, and he said, that's all. He said, he wasn't gonna blow it no more, and he didn't either. So the band…
Yeah. But when was that, Eddie? Do you remember about what period that was?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Hippolyte Charles had Albert Glenny on the bass and had me on his banjo

ctx.x: oh yeah not off the chord but off the music who else was in that band?

David had uh there happened one man that couldn't that wasn't that couldn't come up to par with music that was uh uh Albert Glenny Albert Glenny was the bass player see uh Hippolyte Charles had Albert Glenny on the bass and had me on his banjo
oh I see and who else was there?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1962-01-31
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Albert Glenny? Yeah, I remember Glenny.

ctx.x: He's a lot older than Slowdrag. Oh, yeah. Yeah, I know that old man. Slowdrag's just about, oh, something like 70 this year, I think. I'll be doggone.
The Glenny was 18 years older, yeah.
Whew. Well, there I remember, I can remember him good.
